articles.headline: Police investigating whether Titans DE Harrell assaulted driver before crash
articles.description: Police are investigating whether Titans DE Jaylen Harrell assaulted a rideshare driver before a serious car crash that left him hospitalized.
articles.headlineJa: 警察、タイタンズのDEハレルが事故前に運転手を暴行したか捜査
articles.descriptionJa: 警察は、タイタンズのDEジェイレン・ハレルが、入院を余儀なくされる深刻な自動車事故を起こす前に、配車サービスの運転手を暴行したかどうかを捜査している。
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- Police are investigating whether Tennessee Titans defensive end Jaylen Harrell assaulted a rideshare driver shortly before a serious car crash that left Harrell hospitalized. 

Harrell was in his hometown of Tampa when the crash occurred Friday morning. The Titans said in a statement that he was continuing to receive care in the hospital and they were in constant communication with his family.

Tampa Police said in a statement that Harrell was a passenger in the back seat of a white Kia Sorento "when he reportedly assaulted the driver while the vehicle was in motion."

The driver, a man in his mid-30s, swerved and struck a second vehicle before colliding with a utility pole. Harrell was thrown forward, struck the windshield and lost consciousness, the statement said.

The driver had minor injuries and was treated at the scene, according to police. The driver of the second vehicle, a woman in her early 50s, was not hurt.

The 24-year-old Harrell has not played for the Titans this season. He injured an ACL during the preseason and was placed on season-ending injured reserve.

The Titans asked for privacy for Harrell and his family and said they would "provide an update when appropriate."

Tennessee selected Harrell in the seventh round of the 2024 draft out of Michigan. He finished his rookie season with 13 combined tackles and had 25 last season. He also had 4½ sacks and a forced fumble in 2025.

Harrell's father, James, also played eight seasons in the NFL.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Kyrie Irving scores 25, Cooper Flagg 22 as the Mavericks top the Clippers 110-100
articles.description: — Kyrie Irving scored 25 points and Cooper Flagg had 22 points, eight rebounds and six assists as the Dallas Mavericks used a late 11-0 run to beat the Los Angeles Clippers 110-100 on Saturday night.
articles.headlineJa: カイリー・アービングが25得点、クーパー・フラッグが22得点でマーベリックスがクリッパーズに110-100で勝利
articles.descriptionJa: 土曜夜に行われた試合で、ダラス・マーベリックスは終盤に11-0のランを記録。カイリー・アービングの25得点、クーパー・フラッグの22得点、8リバウンド、6アシストの活躍により、ロサンゼルス・クリッパーズを110-100で破った。
articles.body:
DALLAS -- — Kyrie Irving scored 25 points and Cooper Flagg had 22 points, eight rebounds and six assists as the Dallas Mavericks used a late 11-0 run to beat the Los Angeles Clippers 110-100 on Saturday night.


              Walter Clayton Jr. added 16 points and Max Christie finished with 13, both off the bench, as Dallas (9-7) began a back-to-back with a second consecutive win at home following an 0-3 trip. 


              Brook Lopez scored 17 of his 21 points in the second half to lead the Clippers (4-11), who have dropped three straight overall and are 0-7 on the road. Rui Hachimura had 19 points, matching a season high with four 3-pointers.


              After the Clippers’ Kris Dunn hit a corner 3 that cut Dallas’ lead to 91-88 with 5:12 left, the Mavericks scored 11 in a row aided by two Los Angeles turnovers.


              Irving opened shooting 1 of 7 from the floor but scored 12 points in the fourth quarter.


              Flagg went 7 of 13 at the foul line, the first time last season’s NBA Rookie of the Year — an 84.2% free-throw shooter — has missed six in his brief career.


              Clayton and Christie combined to go 5 of 7 from behind the arc.


              The Clippers entered last in the NBA in rebounding, averaging 39 per game. They beat the Mavericks on the boards 54-52 but were outscored 20-19 in second-chance points.


              The Mavericks played their first game this season without starting forward P.J. Washington Jr., who sat out with an illness.


              Up next
              Clippers: Visit Houston on Monday.


              Mavericks: At Utah on Sunday night to begin a three-game trip.


              ------

articles.headline: DiBernardo joins Rapinoe, Pulisic in pantheon of great Olimpicos
articles.description: Vanessa DiBernardo joined an elite list on Saturday, scoring for Kansas City direct from a corner. Known in soccer circles as an Olimpico, here are some of the very best.
articles.headlineJa: ディベルナルド、ラピノーやプリシッチと共に「オリンピコ」の名手たちに名を連ねる
articles.descriptionJa: バネッサ・ディベルナルドは土曜日、カンザスシティの一員としてコーナーキックから直接ゴールを決め、エリートリストに名を連ねた。サッカー界で「オリンピコ」として知られるこの得点方法における、歴代の名シーンを紹介する。
articles.body:
(Editor's note: This article was originally published on Oct. 2, 2025, and it has been updated after Vanessa DiBernardo's stunner in Saturday's NWSL championship finale.)

For a relatively simple sport, soccer is filled with novelties.

Outfield players don the gloves and go into goal when there's no other option, penalty takers attempt chipped "Panenka" spot kicks to varying degrees of success, goalkeepers sprint the length of the pitch to come up for last-minute corners -- and sometimes they even score. And every now and then, players will score directly from a corner kick.

Highly improbable, sometimes intentional, a goal scored in this way is known as a Gol Olimpico, an Olympic goal.

But how did these goals get their name? The history of the Olimpico is irrevocably intertwined with South American football and with one of its great rivalries: Uruguay vs. Argentina.

- New Premier League record set with eight injury-time goals

- From World Cup Willie to Ciao: Ranking every World Cup mascot

- NWSL has more money than ever, yet its biggest problems remain

On June 9, 1924, Uruguay won the Olympic gold medal in Paris after defeating Switzerland 3-0. Around the same time in June 1924, the International Football Association Board (IFAB) changed the laws around corner kicks, making goals scored directly from the corner legal. But it wasn't until Oct. 2, 1924, that these two pieces of information would combine to create the Olimpico moniker.

Following Uruguay's Olympic victory, they played a two-game friendly series with their South American neighbors Argentina. The teams played out a 1-1 draw in Montevideo in late-September before travelling to Buenos Aires.

The return match was suspended after four minutes due to the large crowd on the sideline and was rescheduled for Oct. 2. Argentina would eventually win the rematch 2-1, but the whole game was filled with controversy. La Celeste withdrew from the match with four minutes remaining and both sides accused the other of excessive aggression.

But the important part of this story happened in the 15th minute, when Argentina's Cesareo Onzari whipped in a corner and scored.

The audacity of the goal and La Albiceleste defeating the Olympic champions was the catalyst for local journalists to dub the goal an Olympic one. From then on, whenever other goals were scored in this fashion, they were described as like the one scored against the Olympians, and soon the label Gol Olimpico was applied to all such goals.

The Olimpico is stunning when it's intentional and sometimes comical when it's not. It really has no right to work considering where players are standing on the field, how much of the target they can see from that position and what they need to do to the ball to make it curve into the back of the net. Whether they dribble through at the near post or sail past everyone into the far corner, there's beauty in the curl of ball, the audacity, the incredulity. It's glorious.

articles.headline: Victor Wembanyama has 50 points, 19 rebounds on dominant night as Spurs roll past Pelicans, 114-91
articles.description: — Victor Wembanyama had 50 points, with 32 coming in the first half, along with 19 rebounds, five blocks and four steals and the San Antonio Spurs rolled to a 114-91 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Saturday.
articles.body:
SAN ANTONIO -- — Victor Wembanyama had 50 points, with 32 coming in the first half, along with 19 rebounds, five blocks and four steals and the San Antonio Spurs rolled to a 114-91 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Saturday.


              Wembanyama is the first player with 30 points, 10 rebounds, three blocks and three steals in a game this season and he did so by halftime.


              Stephon Castle added 19 points, six assists and three rebounds for San Antonio, which has won 14 of 15 to join the Los Angeles Lakers atop the Western Conference at 14-3.


              Jeremiah Fears had 29 points and Jordan Poole added 25 points in New Orleans' third consecutive loss.


              Wembanyama exited shortly after reaching 50 points on a 3-pointer that put San Antonio up 108-82 with 6:29 remaining in the game. He finished two points shy of the career high he set Nov. 4 against Dallas.


              Dylan Harper missed his second straight game with a strained left hip suffered on Tuesday against Detroit in San Antonio’s lone loss since Oct. 23. The Spurs limited their turnovers to 13 after committing a season-high 21 in their first game without Harper. 


              San Antonio outscored New Orleans 82-62 over the final three quarters.


              The Spurs captured a 61-45 lead at halftime after two scuffles in the second quarter.


              Jaron Pierre Jr. shoved Wembanyama from behind after the 7-foot-4 center was fouled by Karlo Matković with 9:27 remaining in the first half. Technical fouls were given to Pierre and Keldon Johnson, who confronted the Pelicans forward after the shove.


              Wembanyama responded by scoring the next seven points, including spinning around Yves Missi for a one-handed slam.


              De'Aaron Fox received a technical and had to be separated with 3:49 remaining in the first half after the Spurs guard gave a two-handed shove to Fears following a backcourt violation on the New Orleans guard.


              Wembanyama again responded, scoring the next five points.


              New Orleans was without Zion Williamson (bruised left thigh), Trey Murphy III (knee) and Bennedict Mathurin (left plantar fasciitis). Former Spurs point guard Dejounte Murray remains away from the Pelicans after having his agent, Rich Paul, request a trade from New Orleans on Nov. 13.


              Up next
              Pelicans: Host Phoenix on Monday.


              Spurs: At Sacramento on Monday.


              ------

articles.headline: Brunson scores 30, Bridges hits 3 at buzzer, lifting Knicks to 97-96 win over Trail Blazers
articles.description: — Jalen Brunson scored 30 points, Mikel Bridges hit the winning 3-pointer at the buzzer, and the New York Knicks edged the Portland Trail Blazers 97-96 on Saturday night.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- — Jalen Brunson scored 30 points, Mikel Bridges hit the winning 3-pointer at the buzzer, and the New York Knicks edged the Portland Trail Blazers 97-96 on Saturday night.


              The defending champions led by 26 points in the first half before Portland charged back and took a 96-94 lead with 3.4 seconds left after a pair of free throws from Deni Avdija.


              New York called a timeout to advance the ball past half court and Josh Hart found Bridges on the wing as Toumani Camara leapt past him. Bridges calmly hit his second 3-pointer of the night before he was mobbed by his teammates.


              Brunson scored 19 of his 30 points in the first quarter and Landry Shamet had 20 for the Knicks, who won their fourth consecutive game on a night they honored 50 alumni.


              Donovan Clingan finished with 22 points and 13 rebounds, and Avdija had 20 for Portland, who have lost three of their last four games — all on the road.


              The Knicks led 66-43 at the break — the fewest points they have allowed in the first half this season — before Portland mounted its rally.


              The Trail Blazers — whose 43 points over the first two quarters were a season low — outscored New York 29-15 in the third period and cut the deficit to six points with 58 seconds remaining in the quarter before Shamet’s 3-pointer extended the Knicks lead to 81-72.


              Portland fell behind by 13 after a 3-point play from Tyler Kolek extended the New York lead 92-79.


              Camara and Lillard scored consecutive baskets before Jose Alvarado’s layup made it 94-84.


              Lillard then sparked a 12-0 run capped by Advija’s free throws after he was fouled by Andre Drummond, who attempted to strip the ball away, before Bridges’ last-second 3.


              Up Next
              Trail Blazers: Visit Philadelphia on Monday night.


              Knicks: Host Indiana on Sunday night.


              ------

articles.headline: Jaden McDaniels scores 25 and Timberwolves top short-handed Grizzlies 104-95
articles.description: — Jaden McDaniels scored 25 points, Ayo Dosunmu added 19 and the Minnesota Timberwolves beat the short-handed Memphis Grizzlies 104-95 on Saturday night.
articles.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- — Jaden McDaniels scored 25 points, Ayo Dosunmu added 19 and the Minnesota Timberwolves beat the short-handed Memphis Grizzlies 104-95 on Saturday night.


              Jonathan Kuminga scored 16 points, Terrence Shannon Jr. added 15 and LaMelo Ball had 12 as Minnesota shot a season-high 58% from the field.


              Minnesota has won three of four; however, it continues searching for consistent offensive flow without injured Anthony Edwards. The Timberwolves had 23 turnovers after having 17 and 21 in its prior two games.


              Cedric Coward tied a season high with 23 points to lead Memphis, which lost for the first time in six games and first time on the road in nine starts. The Grizzlies have the league’s top offensive rating, but recorded season lows in points in a quarter (12), half (46) and game against the league’s top defensive rated team.


              Memphis played without power forward Cam Boozer (right ankle sprain), second on the team with 16.6 points per game to go along with a team-high 9.2 rebounds, and forward Jerami Grant (left calf strain). Coach Tuomas Iisalo said pregame that Boozer was undergoing further evaluations and “there will be a medical update later on” regarding Grant.


              Guard Ty Jerome, averaging a team-high 25.4 points, scored 18 in his first game back after missing four games with a right hip impingement.


              Down by 23 points early in the fourth quarter, Memphis got within 97-90 with 2:37 left, but McDaniels countered with back-to-back layups for Minnesota.


              Minnesota outscored Memphis 28-12 in the second quarter to take control.


              Down by 11 early in the frame, the Timberwolves went on a 26-6 run capped by a Rudy Gobert dunk off a missed Ball free throw on their way to a 56-46 lead at the break.


              Dosunmu had three driving layups as the Timberwolves scored 14 of the final 16 points of the third quarter for an 83-62 advantage.


              Up next
              Grizzlies: At Charlotte on Monday.


              Timberwolves: Host Brooklyn on Monday.


              ------

articles.headline: Sources: Rams' Puka Nacua out 4-5 months after knee surgery, will miss playoffs
articles.description: Puka Nacua's recovery time from MCL surgery is considered to be four to five months, sources told ESPN, meaning he will miss the playoffs.
articles.body:
Puka Nacua's recovery time from MCL surgery is considered to be four to five months, sources told ESPN on Saturday, meaning the Los Angeles Rams star wide receiver will miss the rest of this season, including the playoffs.

Sources told ESPN that three doctors recommended that Nacua undergo the procedure, which is expected to have him healthy for the 2027 campaign.

Nacua's right knee checked out clean aside from the MCL, according to a source. The operation was performed by team doctor Neal ElAttrache, a source told ESPN.

Rams coach Sean McVay said Friday that Nacua, who is serving a three-game suspension while on injured reserve, will likely miss at least the rest of the regular season after undergoing surgery Tuesday.

McVay added that the possibility of Nacua returning for the postseason was a scenario that the Rams "haven't thought about."

The NFL was unaware that Nacua had already undergone surgery when it imposed its suspension, a source told ESPN on Friday.

In seven games this season, Nacua had 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns. The two-time Pro Bowler suffered the knee injury, along with a turf toe injury, on the Rams' final offensive snap of their Week 9 victory over the Washington Commanders and was placed on IR on Nov. 12.

Nacua, 25, is playing on the final year of his rookie deal and is scheduled to be an unrestricted free agent this offseason.

articles.headline: Carlos Espí's 'most special' goal earns Real Madrid win and Rafael Nadal praise
articles.description: Real Madrid supersub Carlos Espí said his late goal against Celta Vigo was his "most special" yet after earning his team the win and praise from Rafael Nadal.
articles.body:
MADRID -- Real Madrid supersub Carlos Espí said his 85th-minute winner against Celta Vigo was his "most special" goal yet for the club after earning his team all three points at the Bernabéu on Saturday.

Celta's Pablo Durán put the visitors ahead after just six minutes, before a late rally saw Jude Bellingham level for Madrid, and then Espí -- who was introduced on 79 minutes by coach José Mourinho -- score from close range, after Vinícius Júnior's cross, to seal a 2-1 victory.

- Madrid chief Pérez: "outrageous" that LaLiga president Tebas hasn't resigned

- Hunter: Has Vini Jr. finally put summer transfer saga behind him? Real Madrid need him at his best

Espí, 21, has played just 44 minutes for Madrid in LaLiga this season but he's now scored three, crucial goals to secure victories against Espanyol, Elche and Celta, as well as netting in the club's 4-3 Champions League comeback win away at Roma.

"I think it's the most special," Espí told reporters on Saturday, when asked about his first goal scored in front of the Bernabéu crowd.

"Honestly, it's a day I'll never forget ... I can't even count how many times I've dreamed of scoring here, celebrating with the fans, and hearing them chant my name."

Espí said coach Mourinho was "euphoric" after his late winner, and described meeting Rafael Nadal post-match, after the tennis legend was voted onto Madrid's board of directors earlier on Saturday.

"I went over to see [Nadal], and he was very proud of me," Espí said. "Having a legend like Rafa Nadal there, talking to me, it made me incredibly happy."

Mourinho cited the return from the international break as a factor in Madrid's lackluster first-half performance, which saw them trail at halftime.

"If you look at the big teams that played today: Arsenal didn't win, [Manchester] City didn't win, Chelsea didn't win, Bayern [Munich] didn't win," Mourinho said. "It's difficult."

Mourinho confirmed that Vinícius -- who he brought off the bench after 57 minutes on Saturday -- would start in Madrid's Champions League game with PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday.

The coach also revealed why Espí is unlikely to start many games alongside first-choice center forward Kylian Mbappé.

"It's possible, but when we lose the ball, I -- on the touchline -- would have to run onto the pitch during the transition, and clatter someone on the opposing team," Mourinho joked.

"Playing with two pure forwards means your wingers have to be very capable of defending in central areas. And that wouldn't be Vinícius, for sure. Arda [Güler] might do it a bit, Brahim [Díaz] a bit, but given the characteristics of our wingers, we aren't built to play in a traditional 4-4-2."

articles.headline: David Raya to be assessed after leaving Arsenal's draw at Newcastle with injury
articles.description: David Raya was forced off with an injury during Arsenal's 2-2 draw at Newcastle United on Saturday.
articles.headlineJa: ダビド・ラヤ、ニューカッスル戦の引き分け中に負傷交代、状態を確認へ
articles.descriptionJa: 土曜日のニューカッスル・ユナイテッドとの対戦で、アーセナルのダビド・ラヤが負傷により途中交代を余儀なくされた。
articles.body:
David Raya was forced off with an injury during Arsenal's 2-2 draw at Newcastle United on Saturday.

The Spain goalkeeper walked off holding his left arm and looked in discomfort as he did so. He was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

"Unfortunately, he had to come off which is never good news," Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta said. "He will get assessed now and he will probably have an MRI tomorrow to see what it is exactly because at the moment I don't know.

"It was a knock. I don't know how it happened or what the injury is at the moment so we'll have to see wait and see tomorrow.

"We know how important David is for us but tomorrow we will have more news."

The 31-year-old had played every minute of Arsenal's Premier League and Champions League games this season up to that point.

He also played 37 out of Arsenal's 38 games as they lifted the Premier League last season.

Raya has won the league's Golden Glove award in each of the last three seasons, and Arsenal have conceded the joint-fewest goals so far this Premier League season.

The Spaniard could join Bukayo Saka and Martín Zubimendi on the sidelines, although Saturday's game did see William Saliba feature in a Premier League squad for the first time this season.

- Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal: Noni Madueke rescues point for Gunners against spirited hosts - as it happened

- Mikel Arteta: Steps taken to avoid team leaks due to Fantasy Premier League

- Andoni Iraola, Mikel Arteta warn of drone risk after Man United incident

Arsenal opened the scoring through Eberechi Eze on Saturday but found themselves behind midway through the second half thanks to goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw, before Noni Madueke rescued a point for the visitors.

The result saw Arteta's side go six points clear at the top of the table.

ESPN's James Olley contributed to reporting.

articles.headline: Chelsea in 'fragile moment' as Caicedo injury adds to pain of Leeds rout
articles.description: Another crisis might be unfolding at Chelsea, just a few months into Xabi Alonso's tenure.
articles.headlineJa: チェルシー、カイセドの負傷がリーズ戦の大敗に追い打ち、「脆い局面」に直面
articles.descriptionJa: シャビ・アロンソ監督の就任からわずか数ヶ月、チェルシーでは再び危機が訪れている可能性がある。
articles.body:
Home defeats to big rivals. Injuries to key players. One of the worst defenses in the Premier League.

Another crisis might be unfolding at Chelsea, just a few months into Xabi Alonso's tenure.

- Raya exits with injury as Arsenal held by Newcastle: 'Never good news'

- Man City at a crossroads as a shell of themselves

- VAR review: Should Haaland's goal vs Fulham have been disallowed

"We're in a fragile moment," Alonso said Saturday after seeing his team overrun in a 4-1 home loss to Leeds, who hadn't won at Stamford Bridge this century.

"We need to be tougher," he added. "It's something mandatory in this competition.

Already without major players in striker João Pedro and defender Maxence Lacroix because of injuries, Chelsea fell apart against Leeds following the enforced withdrawal of Moisés Caicedo in the 22nd minute after the Ecuador midfielder landed awkwardly on his back while making a challenge.

Despite going ahead within three minutes through Emmanuel Emegha on his first start, Leeds equalized almost immediately through Noah Okafor and dominated the second half, scoring through Dominic Calvert-Lewin -- via the penalty spot -- Okafor again and then U.S. midfielder Brenden Aaronson.

Leeds -- whose rivalry with Chelsea dates back to the 1960s and early '70s -- last beat the London club away in 1999. Less than a month ago, Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018. Before the international break, Chelsea lost 1-0 at Sunderland, which started that match in last place.

Chelsea, one of the biggest spenders in Europe in recent seasons, has tumbled toward midtable and are putting in lethargic performances even though the team doesn't have the hindrance of European competition this season.

"After we lost Moises, we lost completely the momentum," Alonso said. "Until then we were doing OK, but from that moment they started believing and we started not believing. After that, we never got the good feeling and were not able to come from the pressure. It completely changed.

"I'm not feeling [let down]. We do it as a team, as [a] collective. We need to support each other. We need to find solutions to do better because this will happen. There were moments that we were not competing at the level required. But the physicality, the duels, it's not the only explanation. The mentality part we can do better."

Chelsea has now conceded 20 goals in 11 games, with only last-place Crystal Palace and promoted teams Ipswich and Coventry letting in more.

Information from The Associated Press and PA contributed to this report.

articles.headline: PSG star Désiré Doué suffers 'serious' knee injury in win over Nice
articles.description: PSG forward Désiré Doué was carried off on a stretcher with a serious knee injury late in the first half of the team's 3-2 win at Nice in Ligue 1 on Saturday.
articles.headlineJa: PSGのスター、デジレ・ドゥエがニース戦の勝利の中で「深刻な」膝の負傷
articles.descriptionJa: 土曜日に行われたリーグ・アンのニース戦（3-2でPSGが勝利）の後半、PSGフォワードのデジレ・ドゥエが深刻な膝の負傷により担架で運び出された。
articles.body:
Paris Saint-Germain forward Désiré Doué was carried off on a stretcher with a serious knee injury late in the first half of the team's 3-2 win at Nice in Ligue 1 on Saturday.

The defending champions' 12th straight win in all competitions was soured by yet another injury.

"We will have to wait until tomorrow to know the exact nature of the injury. But it is a serious injury, we have seen the images," PSG coach Luis Enrique said after the game. "That's the life of a professional footballer, you have to realize that this is part of a career and you have to accept it."

It happened when he turned to shield the ball from Nice midfielder Sofiane Diop and his fully-extended leg buckled under him without any contact from Diop.

The France forward fell to the ground clutching his right knee in the 39th minute and looked in severe pain as he cried out. Moments later he was taken off on a stretcher and placed both hands on his face.

"He is sad and worried," Luis Enrique said. "He will come back twice as strong, I have no doubt."

The 21-year-old Doué -- who shot to prominence with an outstanding performance in the 2025 Champions League win against Inter Milan -- had scored his second league goal of the season earlier in the first half.

Spain forward Ferran Torres replaced him and scored the third goal. Senny Mayulu got PSG's opening goal.

Two-time defending champions PSG face Roma in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Doué missed stretches of last season with a calf strain and a thigh injury and had a bothersome ankle injury the previous season.

His latest injury is a concern for Enrique, after Khvicha Kvaratskhelia tore the ACL in his right knee against Barcelona on Oct. 20 and Ousmane Dembélé and captain Marquinhos tore thigh muscles in that game.

Dembélé came off the bench against Nice in the second half for PSG.

Information from The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.description: Scott McTominay's second-half strike earned Napoli a hard-fought 1-0 win over Torino to ease the pressure on manager Massimiliano Allegri.
articles.headlineJa: スコット・マクトミナイがトリノを撃破、ナポリの3試合未勝利を止める
articles.descriptionJa: スコット・マクトミナイが後半にゴールを決め、ナポリはトリノに1-0で苦戦の末に勝利し、マッシミリアーノ・アッレグリ監督への重圧を軽減した。
articles.body:
Scott McTominay's second-half strike earned Napoli a hard-fought 1-0 win over Torino to ease the pressure on manager Massimiliano Allegri.

With a run of one league win in five, Allegri had found himself under the spotlight and it looked set to be another frustrating night for the Partenopei as Torino goalkeeper Lucas Perri made a string of fine saves.

Scotland midfielder McTominay eventually beat the on-loan Leeds man with a low strike from the edge of the area in the 73rd minute as Napoli closed back up on the top six.

Napoli had made a bright start, with Matteo Politano's low drive parried out by Perri before McTominay then saw his deflected strike tipped around the far post.

Perri thwarted Napoli again when he made a flying save to push away Rasmus Højlund's drive.

Højlund then headed over before Kevin De Bruyne -- on as an early substitute following injury to Antonio Vergara -- saw his diving header blocked by Torino defender Saúl Coco.

Torino almost snatched the lead just before halftime when a rising, long-range effort from Rolando Mandragora crashed against the crossbar.

The visitors went close again at the start of the second half as Zakaria Aboukhlal flashed an angled drive from the right across the face of goal before Nikola Vlasic fired over at the far post.

Perri palmed out McTominay's 20-yard drive and Napoli keeper Vanja Milinkovic-Savic then got down to push away Mandragora's curling free-kick.

McTominay eventually broke Torino's resistance with 17 minutes left.

Substitute Noa Lang set off on a counter-attack down the left before laying the ball off to McTominay, who strode forwards to drill an angled drive into the bottom corner.

articles.headline: Cardinals rule out rookie Carson Beck, turn to 40-year-old Josh Johnson vs. Chiefs
articles.description: Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck has been downgraded to out, paving the way for 40-year-old Josh Johnson to start against the Chiefs.
articles.body:
Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, paving the way for 40-year-old Josh Johnson to get his first start for Arizona.

Coach Mike LaFleur said Friday that Arizona was preparing Johnson to start after Beck experienced back spasms again this week. Beck didn't practice Thursday or Friday after being a limited participant Wednesday.

Sunday against the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium will be Johnson's first start since Week 18 of last season and just his 12th career start after being a fifth-round pick in 2008. He is 2-9 overall.

Although he doesn't have a lot of starting experience compared with his longevity in the league -- Arizona is his 15th NFL team -- the situation Johnson is in feels "familiar."

"It's kind of my testimony my whole life, just the unknown, what can happen," Johnson said. "And so just always just being in the moment, being prepared for myself. I've been in this situation, particularly in the NFL, a lot. So more excited than nerves, I would say."

Johnson said he is in a constant state of staying ready, which has been a factor in him playing into his 40s. At this point in his career, he's used to it.

Last season, Johnson replaced injured Washington Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota in Week 16 and then started the final two games of the season after not starting since 2021.

"My job is to always be ready no matter what, no matter how the situation," Johnson said. "So I focus more on that than what's not ideal. And so this is just the next step of that process, and it keeps happening and so you just keep accepting it. You don't fight it, you embrace it, and you just go with it."

Johnson said his experience working with LaFleur in 2020 when LaFleur was the San Francisco 49ers' receivers coach and in 2021 with the New York Jets when LaFleur was the offensive coordinator will help "tremendously" on Sunday.

"Just understanding how he calls the game first and foremost is very important because you don't have to get antsy, like, 'Oh, what is he going to do in these moments?'" Johnson said. "And Mike is pretty consistent. He's been consistent. I've always been a big fan of him as a playcaller, as a coach, just in general."

Johnson is also familiar with Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo, having played against him and being on the Giants when Spagnuolo was New York's defensive coordinator in 2016.

Despite a familiarity and comfort with LaFleur, Johnson is also realistic about how Sunday can go after spending less than two weeks learning the offense.

"I also understand that everything ain't going to be perfect," Johnson said. "I'm not trying to go out there and be perfect. I'm trying to go out there and play winning football."

articles.headline: Steelers activate WR Roman Wilson off IR for Eagles game
articles.description: The Steelers have activated wide receiver Roman Wilson from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles.
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH -- The Steelers have activated wide receiver Roman Wilson from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Fellow wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr., though, was not activated from injured reserve. The Steelers will also be without outside linebacker Nick Herbig, who was downgraded to out with a hip/ribs injury Saturday.

The Steelers elevated practice squad wide receiver Max Hurleman after the former undrafted free agent earned votes of confidence from quarterback Aaron Rodgers and coach Mike McCarthy over the past two weeks. They also signed linebacker KJ Henry to the active roster to help replace Herbig.

Wilson has been out since fracturing one finger and dislocating another in the Steelers' Week 5 win against the Indianapolis Colts. His return figures to boost the Steelers' sluggish passing game and could help alleviate the attention on top receiver DK Metcalf, who has struggled throughout the season.

A 2024 third-round pick, Wilson was developing into a reliable deep threat prior to his injury, with touchdowns in back-to-back games for the first time in his career.

"Instead of having four receivers up, we'll probably have five or six," Metcalf said Thursday. "So I mean a lot more rotation, a lot of fresh bodies. But just watching them out there at practice these past couple days, they look fresh, they look ready to go to me."

Wilson had his 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve opened earlier this week and was a full participant in practice each day this week.

articles.headline: Fantasy football Week 11 inactives: Who's in and who's out?
articles.description: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.
articles.body:
Biggest injury concerns for Week 11

Players with early starts

Carson Beck, QB, Cardinals (back): Beck popped up on Thursday's injury report with a back injury. He has dealt with this issue throughout the season and currently appears to be unlikely to play in Week 11. Josh Johnson would be next man up and is purely a two-QB format option for those who are desperately in need of a bye week/injury replacement. In either event, Trey McBride is the only Cardinals player who should be started with any confidence -- and even his value is diminished in this new-look Cardinals offense.

Dalton Kincaid, TE, Bills (thumb/ankle): Kincaid has not yet practiced this week and is doubtful for Week 11. With the Bills playing the Chiefs on Thanksgiving -- just four days after this game -- expect Buffalo to use caution here. If he sits, Dawson Knox becomes a deeper streaming option against a Dolphins team that has allowed the fifth-most TE fantasy PPG.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 11 Buzz 

Week 11 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 11

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Jonathon Brooks, RB, Panthers (groin): Brooks is questionable for Week 11 but seems close to making his return after having practiced in full all week. He is worth adding if he is available on your league's waiver wire, but fantasy managers should take a wait-and-see approach. Chuba Hubbard remains an RB1 play.

Darren Waller, TE, Panthers (knee): Waller is questionable for Week 11 after limited practices Thursday and Friday. Waller is a TD-dependent streaming option. Some preferred TE plays are Mark Andrews and Chig Okonkwo. Waller should be used over Brenton Strange, Dallas Goedert and Mike Gesicki.

Kyle Monangai, RB, Bears (toe): Monangai is off the injury report, meaning he will play in week 11. He has not played since Week 4. Still, he is in the mix as a flex option due to a matchup against the Saints. New Orleans has allowed the fourth-most rushing yards to RBs, as well as the second-most RB fantasy points.

Caleb Douglas, WR, Dolphins (shoulder): Douglas had been limited at practice this week before elevating to full on Friday. He is off the injury report, meaning he will play in Week 11. He has seen eight targets in both of his last two games and has scored double-digit fantasy points in three of his four games since returning from injury. While he is more volatile with QB Kyle McCord, Douglas is in the flex conversation, especially given all the byes.

Jordyn Tyson, WR, Saints (chest): Tyson has been limited at practice this week and is questionable for Week 11. If he plays, he'd be a WR3 (with a lot more upside). articles.headline: Titans DL Jaylen Harrell hospitalized after car accident in Tampa
articles.description: Titans defensive lineman Jaylen Harrell was involved in a serious car accident Friday and remains hospitalized, according to the team.
articles.headlineJa: タイタンズのDLジェイレン・ハレル、タンパでの自動車事故で入院
articles.descriptionJa: チームの発表によると、タイタンズのディフェンシブラインマン、ジェイレン・ハレルが金曜日に深刻な自動車事故に遭い、現在も入院している。
articles.body:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- Tennessee Titans defensive lineman Jaylen Harrell was involved in a serious car accident Friday and remains hospitalized, according to the team.

Harrell, 24, was a passenger in an Uber in Tampa, Florida, when the accident occurred. No further details were available.

"Yesterday, Jaylen Harrell was involved in a serious car accident that resulted in him being taken to the hospital in his hometown of Tampa, Florida," the Titans said in a statement. "We have been in constant communication with Jaylen's family and are still working to gather more information.

"At this time, Jaylen remains in the hospital and continues to receive care. We ask that Jaylen and his family's privacy be respected at this time. We will provide an update when appropriate."

Harrell tore his ACL in the preseason and was placed on season-ending injured reserve. The Titans selected Harrell in the seventh round of the 2024 draft, and he finished his rookie season with 13 combined tackles.

He started two games for Tennessee in 2025 and 25 combined tackles, including 4.5 sacks and a forced fumble.
